newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO LSWR BULLISH, NAPHTHA GAINS FOR SECOND DAY.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO LSWR BULLISH, NAPHTHA GAINS FOR SECOND DAY.

text.p: Low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) was notionally firm in afternoon Tokyo trade on Wednesday, buoyed by a spell of hot weather, while naphtha gained ground for a second consecutive day, oil product traders said.
"Quite a few of our clients asked us to move the delivery timing of their cargoes forward as the hot weather pushed up LSWR demand," one trader said.
A heatwave usually gives a bullish tone to the LSWR market as low sulphur fuel oil in Japan is mainly used at thermal power plants to generate electricity.
Open-spec naphtha was quoted at $207.00/$207.50 per tonne for second-half October delivery, compared with late Tuesday's $206.00/$206.50.

The shutdown of Showa Yokkaichi Sekiyu's 150,000 barrel-per-day topper in central Japan had little impact on domestic oil market as oil product stocks were persistently high at most refineries in Japan, traders said.
The refiner said the topper, which was closed as a result of a minor fire on Monday, is expected to resume operations on August 17.
